subject: E-Governance
description: Comprehensive question bank for Karnataka FDA & SDA examinations covering E-Governance - based on official notes. All points from the source material covered without duplication.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is e-Governance?

options.A: Use of ICT by government institutions to deliver services, exchange information, improve administration, increase transparency and enable citizen participation
options.B: Use of only computers by government offices for typing letters
options.C: A system where citizens govern themselves without government
options.D: Use of social media by government officials for personal communication

questions.explanation: E-Governance is the use of information and communication technology (ICT), especially computers, internet, mobile networks and digital platforms, by government institutions to deliver services, exchange information, improve administration, increase transparency and enable citizen participation.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the difference between e-Government and e-Governance?

options.A: They are exactly the same thing
options.B: E-Government refers to use of ICT to provide government information and services; E-Governance is broader and includes institutional processes, accountability, participation, coordination, decision-making and relationships
options.C: E-Government is for central government only; E-Governance is for state government only
options.D: E-Government is older than e-Governance with no other difference

questions.explanation: E-Government generally refers to the use of ICT to provide government information and services. E-Governance is broader: it also includes institutional processes, accountability, participation, coordination, decision-making and the relationship between government, citizens, businesses and employees.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the main purpose of e-Governance?

options.A: To increase paperwork in government offices
options.B: To make government administration more efficient, transparent, accountable, accessible, responsive, reliable and citizen-centric
options.C: To replace all government employees with computers
options.D: To reduce the number of government services available to citizens

questions.explanation: The main purpose of e-Governance is to make government administration more efficient, transparent, accountable, accessible, responsive, reliable and citizen-centric.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What does ICT stand for?

options.A: Indian Communication Technology

questions.explanation: ICT stands for Information and Communication Technology. It includes computers, software, telecommunications, networks, internet services, databases and digital communication tools.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is digital government?

options.A: A government that only uses digital currency
options.B: An approach where digital technologies and data are integrated into design and delivery of public policies, administrative processes and public services rather than merely converting paper forms into electronic forms
options.C: A government department that deals only with computer hardware
options.D: A government that operates only through social media

questions.explanation: Digital government is an approach in which digital technologies and data are integrated into the design and delivery of public policies, administrative processes and public services, rather than merely converting paper forms into electronic forms.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is meant by citizen-centric governance?

options.A: Governance designed around the convenience of government officials
options.B: Governance that places citizens' needs, convenience, rights and experience at the centre of public administration and designs services around life events and user requirements
options.C: Governance where only citizens with digital devices can access services
options.D: Governance where citizens must visit government offices for every service

questions.explanation: Citizen-centric governance places citizens' needs, convenience, rights and experience at the centre of public administration and designs services around life events and user requirements.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is meant by paperless governance?

options.A: Governance conducted only through newspapers
options.B: Using electronic files, digital documents, e-signatures, online approvals and digital record systems to reduce or eliminate physical paperwork wherever legally and operationally possible
options.C: Governance where no records are maintained at all
options.D: Governance that uses only recycled paper

questions.explanation: Paperless governance means using electronic files, digital documents, e-signatures, online approvals and digital record systems to reduce or eliminate physical paperwork wherever legally and operationally possible.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is meant by faceless service delivery?

options.A: A service where the applicant's identity is not verified
options.B: A service that minimises or removes the need for direct physical interaction between an applicant and an official by using online applications, electronic verification, workflow systems and digital communication
options.C: A service where government officials hide their identity from citizens
options.D: A service that cannot be accessed by anyone

questions.explanation: Faceless service delivery minimises or removes the need for direct physical interaction between an applicant and an official by using online applications, electronic verification, workflow systems and digital communication.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is cashless government service delivery?

options.A: Government services that provide free cash to citizens
options.B: Enabling fees, taxes and other government payments to be made through digital payment methods such as UPI, net banking, cards and authorised electronic payment systems instead of cash
options.C: Government services that do not involve any payment
options.D: Government services that accept only foreign currency

questions.explanation: Cashless service delivery enables fees, taxes and other government payments to be made through digital payment methods such as UPI, net banking, cards and authorised electronic payment systems instead of cash.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is end-to-end online service delivery?

options.A: A service that is available only at the end of the year
options.B: A service where the complete process from application and document submission to verification, payment, decision, issue of certificate and status tracking is completed electronically to the extent permitted by law
options.C: A service that starts online but must be completed offline
options.D: A service that is delivered only through mobile phones

questions.explanation: End-to-end online service delivery means that the complete service process—from application and document submission to verification, payment, decision, issue of certificate and status tracking—is completed electronically, to the extent permitted by law.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is interoperability in e-Governance?

options.A: The ability of citizens to operate computers
options.B: The ability of different government information systems, departments and databases to exchange data and use the exchanged information effectively through agreed standards, formats and interfaces
options.C: The ability of government officials to work in multiple languages
options.D: The ability to operate a computer without electricity

questions.explanation: Interoperability is the ability of different government information systems, departments and databases to exchange data and use the exchanged information effectively through agreed standards, formats and interfaces.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is a single-window system?

options.A: A computer operating system with only one window
options.B: A system that provides access to multiple government services or departmental processes through one portal or service centre, reducing the need to approach several offices separately
options.C: A government office with only one window for public dealing
options.D: A system where only one citizen can be served at a time

questions.explanation: A single-window system provides access to multiple government services or departmental processes through one portal or service centre, reducing the need to approach several offices separately.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is a government portal?

options.A: A physical gate of a government building
options.B: An official web-based platform through which a government department or institution publishes information and provides online services, applications, payments, downloads, tracking and grievance facilities
options.C: A type of computer hardware used in government offices
options.D: A government employee who handles online services

questions.explanation: A government portal is an official web-based platform through which a government department or institution publishes information and provides online services, applications, payments, downloads, tracking and grievance facilities.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)?

options.A: Physical infrastructure like roads and bridges built with digital technology
options.B: Shared, interoperable digital systems such as digital identity, payment networks and data/document exchange platforms that support delivery of services at population scale
options.C: A type of computer server used only by government
options.D: A social media platform run by the government

questions.explanation: Digital Public Infrastructure consists of shared, interoperable digital systems—such as digital identity, payment networks and data/document exchange platforms—that support delivery of services at population scale.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the difference between digitisation and digitalisation?

options.A: They are exactly the same
options.B: Digitisation converts information from physical/analogue form into digital form (e.g., scanning paper records); Digitalisation uses digital technologies to improve or redesign processes (e.g., online mutation of land records or electronic file approval)
options.C: Digitisation is for documents only; digitalisation is for images only
options.D: Digitisation is done by government; digitalisation is done by private companies only

questions.explanation: Digitisation converts information from physical or analogue form into digital form, such as scanning paper records. Digitalisation uses digital technologies to improve or redesign processes, such as online mutation of land records or electronic file approval.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is Government-to-Citizen (G2C) e-Governance?

options.A: Digital services provided by citizens to government
options.B: Digital services provided by government to individuals such as certificates, pensions, ration-card services, land records, utility payments and welfare scheme applications
options.C: Digital interaction between two government departments
options.D: Digital services provided by government to businesses

questions.explanation: G2C refers to digital services provided by government to individuals, such as certificates, pensions, ration-card services, land records, utility payments and applications for welfare schemes.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is Government-to-Business (G2B) e-Governance?

options.A: Digital services provided by businesses to government
options.B: Digital interactions between government and businesses such as business registration, licences, tax filing, tenders, regulatory approvals and online procurement
options.C: Digital services provided by government to its employees

questions.explanation: G2B refers to digital interactions between government and businesses, such as business registration, licences, tax filing, tenders, regulatory approvals and online procurement.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is Government-to-Government (G2G) e-Governance?

options.A: Digital services provided by government to citizens
options.B: Electronic communication, data exchange and workflow between government departments, ministries, agencies and different levels of government
options.C: Digital services provided by government to businesses
options.D: Digital interaction between citizens and businesses

questions.explanation: G2G refers to electronic communication, data exchange and workflow between government departments, ministries, agencies and different levels of government.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is Government-to-Employee (G2E) e-Governance?

options.A: Digital services provided by employees to government
options.B: Digital services for government employees such as salary slips, leave applications, service records, attendance, pension processing and human-resource management
options.C: Digital interaction between government and private employees
options.D: Digital services provided by government to retired employees only

questions.explanation: G2E refers to digital services for government employees, such as salary slips, leave applications, service records, attendance, pension processing and human-resource management.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: Which e-Governance model is represented by an online birth certificate service?

options.A: G2B

questions.explanation: An online birth certificate service is primarily Government-to-Citizen (G2C) because the government provides a service directly to an individual citizen.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: Which e-Governance model is represented by electronic file movement between two departments?

options.A: G2C

questions.explanation: Electronic file movement between two departments represents Government-to-Government (G2G) because the digital interaction takes place between government institutions.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What are the major objectives of e-Governance?

options.A: Faster service delivery, reduced administrative cost, transparency, accountability, reduced corruption opportunities, improved record management, better coordination, wider access, citizen participation and evidence-based decisions
options.B: Increasing the number of government employees and offices
options.C: Making government services more expensive for citizens
options.D: Reducing the use of technology in government

questions.explanation: The major objectives are faster service delivery, reduced administrative cost, transparency, accountability, reduced corruption opportunities, improved record management, better coordination, wider access, citizen participation and evidence-based decisions.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: How does e-Governance improve transparency?

options.A: By keeping all government information secret
options.B: By publishing rules, eligibility conditions, application status, service timelines, decisions and relevant records online, making administrative actions easier to inspect and reducing information asymmetry
options.C: By allowing only government officials to access information
options.D: By increasing the number of forms citizens must fill

questions.explanation: E-Governance improves transparency by publishing rules, eligibility conditions, application status, service timelines, decisions and relevant records online, making administrative actions easier to inspect and reducing information asymmetry.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: How does e-Governance improve accountability?

options.A: By removing all records of government actions
options.B: Through digital audit trails, time stamps, user logs, workflow histories, service-level monitoring and grievance tracking that help identify responsibility for delay, unauthorised access or improper decisions
options.C: By making government officials unaccountable for their actions
options.D: By reducing the number of government services

questions.explanation: Digital audit trails, time stamps, user logs, workflow histories, service-level monitoring and grievance tracking help identify responsibility for delay, unauthorised access or improper decisions.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: How does e-Governance reduce corruption?

options.A: By eliminating all government officials
options.B: By reducing unnecessary personal contact, discretion, cash handling and opaque procedures; however technology alone cannot eliminate corruption
options.C: By making all government services free
options.D: By removing all laws and regulations

questions.explanation: E-Governance can reduce unnecessary personal contact, discretion, cash handling and opaque procedures. However, technology alone cannot eliminate corruption; sound rules, audits, cybersecurity and effective enforcement are also required.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: How does e-Governance support rural development?

options.A: By providing certificates, welfare applications, agricultural information, land records, banking access and other services closer to rural residents through mobile platforms and assisted service centres
options.B: By forcing rural residents to migrate to cities
options.C: By reducing internet connectivity in rural areas
options.D: By closing all rural government offices

questions.explanation: E-Governance can bring certificates, welfare applications, agricultural information, land records, banking access and other services closer to rural residents through mobile platforms and assisted service centres.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the role of e-Governance in inclusive administration?

options.A: It excludes disadvantaged groups from government services
options.B: It can improve access for remote communities, persons with disabilities, women, senior citizens and disadvantaged groups through accessible design, local-language interfaces, assisted access and multiple service channels
options.C: It provides services only to urban residents
options.D: It requires all citizens to own smartphones

questions.explanation: E-Governance can improve access for remote communities, persons with disabilities, women, senior citizens and disadvantaged groups through accessible design, local-language interfaces, assisted access and multiple service channels.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is evidence-based governance?

options.A: Governance based on personal opinions of officials
options.B: Governance that uses reliable data, statistics, monitoring and evaluation to design policies, allocate resources and assess public programmes
options.C: Governance based on ancient texts only
options.D: Governance that does not require any data

questions.explanation: Evidence-based governance uses reliable data, statistics, monitoring and evaluation to design policies, allocate resources and assess public programmes.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is a digital audit trail?

options.A: A physical path used by auditors to reach government offices
options.B: A time-stamped electronic record of actions performed in a system including who accessed, created, modified, approved or transmitted information
options.C: A trail of digital devices left by government officials
options.D: A list of all government websites

questions.explanation: A digital audit trail is a time-stamped electronic record of actions performed in a system, including who accessed, created, modified, approved or transmitted information.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is a Service-Level Agreement (SLA) in public service delivery?

options.A: An agreement between two citizens
options.B: An agreement that specifies measurable service standards such as time within which an application must be processed, expected quality of service and responsibilities of the service provider

questions.explanation: An SLA specifies measurable service standards, such as the time within which an application must be processed, the expected quality of service and the responsibilities of the service provider.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: Does online availability automatically mean a service is fully online?

options.A: Yes, if a service is on a website it is fully online
options.B: No, a portal may only provide information or accept applications; a service is fully online only when the relevant process, verification and final delivery can be completed electronically
options.C: Yes, all government services are fully online
options.D: No, no government service is fully online

questions.explanation: No. A portal may only provide information or accept applications. A service is fully online only when the relevant process, verification and final delivery can be completed electronically, subject to legal requirements.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is a data centre?

options.A: A government office where data entry operators work
options.B: A facility containing servers, storage, networking equipment, security systems and supporting infrastructure used to store, process and manage digital information and applications
options.C: A centre where citizens go to submit paper forms

questions.explanation: A data centre is a facility containing servers, storage, networking equipment, security systems and supporting infrastructure used to store, process and manage digital information and applications.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is a State Data Centre (SDC)?

options.A: A centre that stores only physical files of state government
options.B: A facility that provides centralised IT infrastructure for hosting state government applications, databases and services, supporting availability, data management, security and continuity of digital services
options.C: A training centre for state government employees
options.D: A centre that manages only state government websites

questions.explanation: A State Data Centre provides centralised IT infrastructure for hosting state government applications, databases and services. It supports availability, data management, security and continuity of digital services.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is a State Wide Area Network (SWAN)?

options.A: A network of roads connecting state capitals
options.B: A government network infrastructure designed to provide secure connectivity among state headquarters, district headquarters, blocks/talks and other government offices
options.C: A social media network for state government employees

questions.explanation: SWAN is a government network infrastructure designed to provide secure connectivity among state headquarters, district headquarters, blocks/talks and other government offices.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the National Knowledge Network (NKN)?

options.A: A network of public libraries
options.B: A high-speed network connecting educational and research institutions and other knowledge institutions to support collaboration and access to advanced network resources
options.C: A television network for educational programmes
options.D: A network of government offices dealing with knowledge management

questions.explanation: The National Knowledge Network is a high-speed network connecting educational and research institutions and other knowledge institutions to support collaboration and access to advanced network resources.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is cloud computing in government?

options.A: Computing done only during cloudy weather
options.B: Provision of computing resources such as servers, storage, databases and software over a network on demand, supporting scalable hosting, shared resources and faster deployment subject to security and data-governance rules
options.C: A type of computer used only in hill stations
options.D: A system where all data is stored in physical files

questions.explanation: Cloud computing provides computing resources—such as servers, storage, databases and software—over a network on demand. Government cloud infrastructure can support scalable hosting, shared resources and faster deployment, subject to security and data-governance rules.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is MeghRaj?

options.A: A government scheme for cloud seeding
options.B: The Government of India's GI Cloud initiative intended to accelerate the delivery of e-services through optimised use of cloud computing in government

questions.explanation: MeghRaj is the Government of India's GI Cloud initiative, intended to accelerate the delivery of e-services through optimised use of cloud computing in government.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the National Informatics Centre (NIC)?

options.A: A private company that sells computers to government
options.B: A Government of India institution under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology that provides ICT and e-Governance support to central and state governments
options.C: A centre that provides information only to citizens
options.D: A network of computer training institutes

questions.explanation: The National Informatics Centre (NIC) is a Government of India institution under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology that provides ICT and e-Governance support to central and state governments.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: In which year was the National Informatics Centre (NIC) established?
questions.explanation: NIC was established in 1976.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the role of NIC in e-Governance?

options.A: It develops and supports government digital platforms, networks, data centres, applications, websites, video-conferencing and secure digital services for government organisations
options.C: It provides internet only to private companies
options.D: It manages only social media accounts of government

questions.explanation: NIC develops and supports government digital platforms, networks, data centres, applications, websites, video-conferencing and secure digital services for government organisations.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is a digital record?

options.A: A record stored only in physical files
options.B: Information created, received, maintained or stored in electronic form such as an electronic file, database entry, scanned document or digitally issued certificate
options.C: A record kept in a digital locker made of metal
options.D: A record that exists only in memory

questions.explanation: A digital record is information created, received, maintained or stored in electronic form, such as an electronic file, database entry, scanned document or digitally issued certificate.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is an electronic office (e-Office)?

options.A: An office with no employees
options.B: An electronic office-management approach that supports digital file creation, movement, noting, approval, correspondence, record management and workflow within government offices
options.C: An office that uses only email
options.D: A virtual office on social media

questions.explanation: e-Office is an electronic office-management approach that supports digital file creation, movement, noting, approval, correspondence, record management and workflow within government offices.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What are the advantages of digital records?

options.A: They can be searched quickly, shared with authorised users, backed up, tracked and preserved systematically; they reduce physical storage and improve retrieval but require access controls, backups, retention rules and reliable metadata
options.B: They never require any security measures
options.C: They cannot be shared with anyone
options.D: They eliminate the need for any record management

questions.explanation: Digital records can be searched quickly, shared with authorised users, backed up, tracked and preserved systematically. They can reduce physical storage and improve retrieval, but require access controls, backups, retention rules and reliable metadata.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is metadata?

options.A: Data about data

questions.explanation: Metadata is data about data. For a digital record, it may include the creator, date of creation, file type, subject, version, access permissions and record identifier.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is a backup?

options.A: A separate copy of data maintained so that information can be restored after accidental deletion, corruption or system failure
options.B: A replacement for the original data
options.D: A government scheme for data storage

questions.explanation: A backup is a separate copy of data maintained so that information can be restored after accidental deletion, corruption or system failure.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is disaster recovery?

options.A: A government scheme for disaster victims
options.B: The planned process of restoring IT systems, applications and data after a major disruption, including recovery procedures, backup arrangements and testing
options.C: A method of recovering deleted files from a computer
options.D: A type of insurance for government buildings

questions.explanation: Disaster recovery is the planned process of restoring IT systems, applications and data after a major disruption. It includes recovery procedures, backup arrangements and testing.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is business continuity in government IT?

options.A: Maintaining or restoring essential public services during and after disruptions such as cyberattacks, power failures, natural disasters or network outages
options.B: A business strategy for private companies
options.C: Continuous operation of government businesses for profit

questions.explanation: Business continuity means maintaining or restoring essential public services during and after disruptions such as cyberattacks, power failures, natural disasters or network outages.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is an API?

options.A: A government certificate
options.B: An Application Programming Interface - a defined mechanism through which software applications communicate and exchange data or functionality

questions.explanation: An Application Programming Interface (API) is a defined mechanism through which software applications communicate and exchange data or functionality.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is API Setu?

options.A: A bridge in Delhi
options.B: A Government of India platform intended to facilitate the publication, discovery and use of APIs by government departments and other approved participants, supporting interoperable digital services
options.C: A type of computer network cable

questions.explanation: API Setu is a Government of India platform intended to facilitate the publication, discovery and use of APIs by government departments and other approved participants, supporting interoperable digital services.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is eSign?

options.A: A signboard displayed electronically
options.B: An electronic signature service that enables a person to sign documents digitally through an approved electronic authentication process subject to applicable law and service rules
options.C: A digital display in government offices

questions.explanation: eSign is an electronic signature service that enables a person to sign documents digitally through an approved electronic authentication process, subject to applicable law and service rules.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is a digital signature?

options.A: A signature made with a digital pen
options.B: A cryptographic method used to authenticate the signer and help verify the integrity of an electronic record using public-key cryptography and a digital signature certificate
options.C: A scanned copy of a handwritten signature

questions.explanation: A digital signature is a cryptographic method used to authenticate the signer and help verify the integrity of an electronic record. It uses public-key cryptography and a digital signature certificate issued under the applicable legal framework.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the difference between an electronic signature and a digital signature?

options.A: They are exactly the same
options.B: Electronic signature is the broader legal/technical category of electronic methods used to authenticate a signatory; a digital signature is a specific cryptographic form of electronic signature
options.C: Electronic signature is more secure than digital signature
options.D: Digital signature is only for government use; electronic signature is for private use

questions.explanation: Electronic signature is the broader legal/technical category of electronic methods used to authenticate a signatory. A digital signature is a specific cryptographic form of electronic signature.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP)?

options.A: A plan approved in May 2006 with the vision of making government services accessible to the common person in their locality through common service delivery outlets while ensuring efficiency, transparency and reliability at affordable cost
options.B: A plan for building national highways

questions.explanation: The National e-Governance Plan was approved in May 2006 with the vision of making government services accessible to the common person in their locality through common service delivery outlets, while ensuring efficiency, transparency and reliability at affordable cost.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the main vision of NeGP?

options.A: To make all government services accessible to the common man in his locality through common service delivery outlets and ensure efficiency, transparency and reliability at affordable costs
options.B: To make all government services available only in cities
options.C: To reduce the number of government services

questions.explanation: The main vision of NeGP is to make all government services accessible to the common man in his locality through common service delivery outlets and ensure efficiency, transparency and reliability at affordable costs.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What are Mission Mode Projects (MMPs) under NeGP?

options.A: Projects for military missions
options.B: Defined e-Governance projects focused on specific government functions or service areas with identified objectives, implementation responsibilities and timelines, including land records, income tax, passports, pensions and e-District services

questions.explanation: MMPs are defined e-Governance projects focused on specific government functions or service areas, with identified objectives, implementation responsibilities and timelines. Examples historically included land records, income tax, passports, pensions and e-District services.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the Digital India programme?

options.A: A programme to distribute free computers
options.B: A flagship programme of the Government of India launched on 1 July 2015 to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy
options.D: A programme for digital currency only

questions.explanation: Digital India is a flagship programme of the Government of India launched on 1 July 2015 to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: Who launched the Digital India programme?

options.A: Prime Minister Narendra Modi

questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Digital India programme on 1 July 2015.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What are the three broad vision areas of Digital India?

options.A: Digital infrastructure as a core utility to every citizen, governance and services on demand, digital empowerment of citizens
options.B: Digital entertainment, digital shopping, digital banking
options.C: Digital agriculture, digital industry, digital services
options.D: Digital education, digital health, digital transport

questions.explanation: The three broad vision areas are: (1) digital infrastructure as a core utility to every citizen, (2) governance and services on demand, and (3) digital empowerment of citizens.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: Which ministry is the nodal ministry for Digital India?

options.A: Ministry of Home Affairs
options.B: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

questions.explanation: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) is the nodal ministry for the Digital India programme.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What does UMANG stand for?

options.A: Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance
options.B: Universal Mobile Access for National Governance
options.C: United Mobile Application for Next Generation
options.D: Unified Management Application for National Governance

questions.explanation: UMANG stands for Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance. It is a unified platform developed by MeitY and the National e-Governance Division (NeGD) to provide access to central, state and other public services through mobile.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: When was UMANG launched?

options.A: 23 November 2017

questions.explanation: UMANG was launched on 23 November 2017 at the fifth Global Conference on Cyberspace in New Delhi.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the main purpose of UMANG?

options.A: To provide a single digital access point for a wide range of government services, helping citizens access services through one platform rather than visiting multiple departmental websites
options.B: To provide free mobile phones to citizens

questions.explanation: UMANG provides a single digital access point for a wide range of government services, helping citizens access services through one platform rather than visiting multiple departmental websites.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is DigiLocker?

options.A: A physical locker facility in banks
options.B: A digital document platform under Digital India that enables citizens to receive, store, access and share authentic digital documents and certificates issued by authorised organisations
options.D: A type of computer storage device

questions.explanation: DigiLocker is a digital document platform under Digital India that enables citizens to receive, store, access and share authentic digital documents and certificates issued by authorised organisations.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: When was DigiLocker launched?

questions.explanation: Kutumba is Karnataka's social registry and entitlement-management initiative intended to integrate resident/family and beneficiary information to support identification of eligible people and more proactive delivery of government benefits.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: Samrakshane is associated with which area?

options.A: Crop insurance

questions.explanation: Samrakshane is an online crop-insurance service platform used in Karnataka for crop-insurance-related processes, including applications/records and claim-related workflows under participating schemes.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of MyGov?

options.A: Citizen engagement in governance through discussions, tasks, polls, surveys, ideas and other engagement activities

questions.explanation: MyGov is a citizen engagement platform of the Government of India that enables people to participate in governance through discussions, tasks, polls, surveys, ideas and other engagement activities.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Government e-Marketplace (GeM)?

options.A: Online public procurement of goods and services by government departments and public organisations

questions.explanation: GeM is an online public procurement platform through which government departments and public organisations procure goods and services, promoting transparency, efficiency and competition.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: The National Scholarship Portal (NSP) supports:

options.A: Online scholarship application, processing, verification and related services for eligible students

questions.explanation: NSP is a national digital platform that supports online scholarship application, processing, verification and related services for eligible students under participating scholarship schemes.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: PFMS is used for:

options.A: Tracking funds, payments, accounting and financial reporting in government programmes

questions.explanation: PFMS is a web-based financial management platform of the Government of India used for tracking funds, payments, accounting and financial reporting in government programmes.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: What is the primary objective of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)?

options.A: To transfer eligible benefits, subsidies or assistance directly to beneficiaries to improve targeting, reduce intermediaries and strengthen transparency

questions.explanation: DBT is a mechanism through which eligible benefits, subsidies or assistance are transferred directly to beneficiaries, commonly into their bank accounts, to improve targeting, reduce intermediaries and strengthen transparency.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: Aadhaar is a:

options.A: 12-digit individual identification number issued by UIDAI to residents of India

questions.explanation: Aadhaar is a 12-digit individual identification number issued by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) to residents of India after prescribed enrolment and verification processes.

questions.subject: E-Governance
questions.question: UMANG was launched at which event?

options.A: Fifth Global Conference on Cyberspace in New Delhi

questions.explanation: UMANG was launched on 23 November 2017 at the fifth Global Conference on Cyberspace in New Delhi.
